zh: 依赖 u→v 的意思是 v 的运行区间严格包含在 u 的区间内（u 先开始、后结束），而不是 v 要等 u 结束才开始。顺着依赖往下，子进程的最早开始只会被父进程推得更晚、最晚结束只会被推得更早；有向环则要求某个开始时刻严格小于自己，必然无解。
初始令 start=S、end=E，按拓扑序从父 u 向子 v 传播：start[v]=max(start[v], start[u]+1)，end[v]=min(end[v], end[u]−1)。这些都是任何可行排程的必要界；若最后每个区间都至少长一个单位，这组端点本身就是可行的，而且同时让每个进程运行得最长，所以最优排程唯一。
用扁平邻接表（head/next 数组）和入度数组建图，把入度为 0 的点放入队列做 Kahn 拓扑排序，弹出时向所有子节点传播上下界并减入度。若出队的点数少于 N（有环）或存在 start≥end，输出 IMPOSSIBLE；否则按 PID 顺序输出全部 N 行。链可能长达一百万，不要用递归。
en: A dependency u→v means v's running interval lies strictly inside u's (u starts earlier and ends later), not that v waits for u to finish. Following the dependencies downward, a child's earliest start can only be pushed later by its parents, and its latest end can only be pushed earlier; a directed cycle would require some start time to be strictly less than itself, so it is always infeasible.

Start with start=S and end=E and propagate from parent u to child v in topological order: start[v]=max(start[v], start[u]+1), end[v]=min(end[v], end[u]−1). These are necessary bounds for every feasible schedule; if every interval is still at least one unit long at the end, these endpoints themselves are feasible and simultaneously make every process run as long as possible, so the optimal schedule is unique.

Build the graph with flat adjacency lists (head/next arrays) and an in-degree array, put the nodes of in-degree 0 into a queue and run Kahn's topological sort, propagating the bounds to every child and decrementing its in-degree when a node is popped. If fewer than N nodes are popped (a cycle) or some start≥end, print IMPOSSIBLE; otherwise print all N lines in PID order. Chains can be a million long, so do not use recursion.

explanationEn:
## Original source and correction of the example

fastprep/Optiver/akuna-print-schedule.md at the pinned commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc states in full: each process has an earliest start S and a latest end E; a dependency u→v requires u to start strictly earlier and end strictly later. Times are integers in 1..1000000, every process runs for at least one unit, and the full schedule is printed for PID 1..N. The original asks for running as long as possible, not for an arbitrary shorter feasible schedule.

The original four-process example [[1,2],[100,2100],[110,2200],[200,2330]] with edges 1→2 and 3→2 cannot be scheduled; this site keeps the full input and corrects the answer to IMPOSSIBLE: process 1 runs within [1,2] at most, the dependency forces process 2 to end at ≤1, while its own start is ≥100. The original output lists only three lines, which neither satisfies these edges nor meets the requirement to output N lines. The second public example is a three-process supplementary example explicitly rebuilt by this site, [[100,2100],[110,2200],[200,2330]] with edges 1→2 and 3→2, whose output is 100 2100, 201 2099, 200 2330; it is not claimed to be the correct output for the original four-process input. The third public example is a single process with an equal-time window added by this site, infeasible because a process must run for at least one unit.

The original itself gives 1≤N≤1000000, 0≤M≤1000000 and 1≤S≤E≤1000000, with no self-loops and no repeated ordered pairs among the edges. It also says Sum of N,M≤1000000 across tests, without making clear whether this is a combined sum or separate sums; this is a total-volume constraint of the original batch interface. This site takes one instance per input, explicitly supports a full million each for N and M, and does not quietly shrink this to N+M≤one million. Converting the original class-style interface to standard input does not change the optimization rule.

## Approach

Every dependency makes the child's running interval lie strictly inside the parent's. Initialize start=S and end=E, then propagate from parent u to child v in topological order: start[v]=max(start[v],start[u]+1), end[v]=min(end[v],end[u]−1). Use an in-degree queue and flat adjacency lists, avoiding recursion on deep chains and per-node container allocation. If there is a cycle, or in the end any start≥end, output IMPOSSIBLE.

## Proof of correctness

A directed cycle requires some start time to be strictly less than itself, so there is no solution. On a DAG, induct in topological order: in any valid schedule, the start s[v]≥S[v] and is greater than the start of every parent, so s[v]≥start[v]; the end e[v]≤E[v] and is less than the end of every parent, so e[v]≤end[v]. The initialization and each max/min step accumulate exactly these necessary bounds.

If start[v]≥end[v], no candidate schedule can let that process run for at least one unit. Conversely, when every interval has positive length and the DAG has no cycle, the computed endpoints themselves satisfy the windows and every dependency, so they are all feasible together. Node by node, they contain the interval of any feasible schedule, so they simultaneously maximize the running time of every process, and there is no trade-off where extending one process forces shortening another. Reaching the maximum length requires both endpoints to equal these bounds, so the optimal schedule is unique and can be judged exactly by tokens. This spells out the original requirement to run as long as possible; it does not introduce a new objective such as total profit, lexicographic order or picking an arbitrary solution.

## Complexity and resources

Topological sorting handles every node and edge once: time O(N+M), space O(N+M). Five int arrays of length N and two of length M take about 20N+8M bytes, about 28MB at N=M=one million, plus only the standard input and output buffers. The computed endpoints lie within about [−1000000,2000000], so signed 32-bit integers suffice; recursion is avoided because the longest chain can reach a million. The package supports the full ranges and runs natively in C++ with 3 seconds / 256MiB; final Linux sandbox acceptance is done separately, and local timings are not sandbox evidence.

## Independent verification

For small domains, the oracle directly enumerates every positive-length integer sub-interval of each process, filters by all dependencies, then takes the earliest start and the latest end of the valid set separately, and verifies that they can be combined into a valid schedule together; it does not call topological propagation. The 163 unique small inputs and the extra small-domain exhaustive checks all use this independent enumeration. Formal full-scale cases get independently derived expected outputs from mathematical constructions: windows unchanged without edges, node i of a chain getting [i,1000001−i], an overly long chain being impossible, the child layer of a two-layer complete bipartite graph getting [2,999999], and graphs with cycles being impossible. There are also randomly relabeled DAGs whose bounds come from a closure over full path lengths, independent of the reference's in-degree queue.

The two negative controls respectively drop the strict difference of 1 and forget to propagate the end bound; each must exit normally on all formal inputs to count as killed. The correction of the original example, the single-instance serialization and the explanation of the batch ranges are all publicly disclosed.
